central_question: When whole graduated G2 composites are used as units in the next uplift, is inherited CAPS7 sufficient, or can an admitted higher-level context distinguish G2 units that share CAPS7 but have different intrinsic G1-unit incidence topology?
g3_unit_definition: Any complete finite connected graduated G2 construction term, treated atomically at the inherited G2 public interface while retaining exact internal G1-unit incidence only as hidden challenge evidence.

initial_public_observer.rule: Do not promote incidence topology, diameter, shell profile, degree sequence, articulation structure, construction digest, owner witness, or toric coordinates into the G3 public interface before a registered context-read experiment earns them.

outcome_partition_for_future_S1.REVIEW_REQUIRED: A distinction appears but cannot be attributed to an allowed public structural read without hidden provenance or post-hoc observer changes.
outcome_partition_for_future_S1.TOPOLOGY_NOT_READ: Every admitted S1 context factors through CAPS7 for the frozen challenge domain.
outcome_partition_for_future_S1.TOPOLOGY_READ_EARNED: At least one preregistered context separates equal-CAPS7 G2 units; isolate the smallest invariant needed before promotion.

stage_ladder.question: Freeze complete G2 units, extract inherited CAPS7 public interfaces, and reproduce a same-CAPS7/different-topology challenge corpus without exposing topology.
Apply the same admitted whole-unit connection contexts to interface-colliding G2 units and test whether topology is operationally read.
If S1 produces distinctions, quotient pair outcomes and identify the minimal relabel-invariant added read; otherwise certify the stronger CAPS7 quotient at the tested pair observer.
Test higher-order compatibility/irreducibility after the S2 quotient.
Test composition closure of the resulting G3 candidate units.
Earn a finite G3 read/write descriptor if one exists.
Test recursive closure and graduation; only this gate may authorize G3 graduation.
